items.title: Ray Vega interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 20, 2023
items.q: There’s that Spanish kid, there’s that Puerto Rican kid.” Then I go to Puerto Rico and family members will go, “There’s Ralph’s son the American.”

ctx.x: When you were a kid, was there a distinction between young men and women born in Puerto Rico and those whose parents were born but came to —

I always found it interesting where in New York City they would say, “Hey, there’s that Spanish kid, there’s that Puerto Rican kid.” Then I go to Puerto Rico and family members will go, “There’s Ralph’s son the American.” You know so it was always very confusing. But you know my parents were of the generation that came in in the 1940s, the latter part of the 40s, early 50s. And so when we were being raised in the projects we lived in predominantly African-American community in the projects in the South Bronx and…

Dave Valentin, when I interviewed him, he said, this is a quote, he said, “My parents are from Puerto Rico, they migrated to New York and settled in the original South Bronx. It was a wonderful New York neighborhood, a mixed neighborhood, Italian, Jews, Greeks and Puerto Ricans, and a whole true community where there was really no problem getting along at all.” And he said, “I think they brought the old values into the community: be nice and do the right thing.”
